title: shawk / Impact
description: What removing a host would break: its dependents in the time range, how often they use it, and whether the host was watched. Only TCP, UDP and Unix stream sockets are observed; RDMA (InfiniBand, RoCE) is not.

list.name: host
list.label: Host
list.query: SELECT host FROM shawk_v1.agents UNION SELECT host FROM shawk_v1.inventory ORDER BY 1
list.definition: SELECT host FROM shawk_v1.agents UNION SELECT host FROM shawk_v1.inventory ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Verdict

targets.rawSql:
SELECT verdict, array_to_string(reasons, ', ') AS reasons, array_to_string(caveats, ', ') AS caveats,
       direct AS dependents, transitive AS dependents_of_dependents, coverage * 100 AS coverage_percent,
       unobserved AS not_observed, gaps, partly_observed AS dropped_flows_for
FROM shawk_v1.impact_verdict(${host:sqlstring}, $__timeFrom(), $__timeTo(),
       min_coverage => ${min_coverage:sqlstring}::numeric / 100, max_depth => ${depth:sqlstring}::integer)

panels.description: UNSAFE: the host has dependents in the time range. SAFE: it has none, and its agent observed it for the coverage asked of the time range. INCONCLUSIVE: none was seen, but the host was not watched enough to tell; reasons say what was missing (not_observed, dropped_flows, udp_not_traced, netns_limited; unknown_host or no_agent for a name no agent reported under). caveats are the same shortfalls where they did not decide the verdict. coverage_percent is cut, not rounded: 100 is all of the time range. Only TCP, UDP and Unix stream sockets are observed: a host used over RDMA is not seen to be used. For a service or a port of the host alone, use shawk-impact or shawk_v1.impact_verdict().

panels.title: Dependents

targets.rawSql:
SELECT depth, client_host, client_service, client_addr, server_host, server_service, port, proto, observed_by,
       cadence, period, runs, last_seen, next_expected
FROM shawk_v1.impact(${host:sqlstring}, $__timeFrom(), $__timeTo(), max_depth => ${depth:sqlstring}::integer)
LIMIT 1000

panels.description: The clients of the host (depth 1), and the clients of its dependents after, each at the depth it is first reached. A client without an agent has client_addr, and the host the inventory gives the address. port 0 stands for the ports of a service under the rules of ports. cadence is read from the hours in which the dependency was active: continuous breaks at once; daily, weekly, monthly and periodic at their next run, which next_expected estimates; one-off and dormant stopped in the time range; unknown has too little history, or hours that were not recorded. At most 1000 rows.

panels.title: Observation of the host

targets.rawSql:
SELECT host, agent, observed * 100 AS observed_percent, unobserved AS not_observed, gaps,
       partly_observed AS dropped_flows_for, dropped_flows, udp_untraced AS without_udp,
       unix_untraced AS without_unix_sockets, netns_limited AS one_netns_only
FROM shawk_v1.coverage($__timeFrom(), $__timeTo(), ARRAY[${host:sqlstring}])

panels.description: How much of the time range the agent of the host observed, and what it did not trace. agent is false for a name no agent ever reported under: such a host is never SAFE.

panels.title: Gaps of the host

targets.rawSql:
SELECT gap_start, gap_end, gap_end - gap_start AS duration, cause, node_state, reason
FROM shawk_v1.unobserved_reasons($__timeFrom(), $__timeTo())
WHERE host = ${host:sqlstring}
ORDER BY gap_start DESC
LIMIT 100

panels.description: The periods in which the host was not observed, with what explains them: cause is maintenance or power_saving for a planned stop. A planned stop is a gap all the same: nothing watched the host then.
